title: Calibrated Confidence Elicitation Improves Falsifiability of LLM Agent Claims
topic: calibration and falsifiability of LLM agents
abstract: We demonstrate that structured confidence elicitation improves calibration error by 18% across three agent benchmarks. Our results show that staked-claim protocols make agent assertions falsifiable and reproducible.

title: On the Reliability of Self-Reported Confidence in Language Model Agents
topic: calibration and falsifiability of LLM agents
abstract: Self-reported confidence in LLM agents fails to correlate with task accuracy and cannot be reproduced under distribution shift. We show agents underperform calibrated baselines by 12% on held-out tasks.

title: A Replication Study of Staked-Claim Calibration in Autonomous Agents
topic: calibration and falsifiability of LLM agents
abstract: We replicate and confirm prior reports that staked-claim protocols improve calibration: our reanalysis demonstrates a consistent 15% reduction in expected calibration error, validating the original finding.

title: Hidden Node Detection via Residual Correlation in Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
topic: hidden variable detection / causal discovery from residuals
abstract: We show that correlating model residuals with exogenous time series detects hidden variables with 91% precision when |r| > 0.5 and mean residual magnitude exceeds 0.1.

title: Residual-Based Causal Discovery Might Sometimes Hint at Latent Structure
topic: hidden variable detection / causal discovery from residuals
abstract: Residual analysis could perhaps, in some sense, hint at latent causal structure, though we believe the connection may remain elusive and we do not commit to a measurable criterion.
